text:
In a town at the foot of a mountain, a lantern seller named Omar had a shop that was always busy during the long winter nights. His lanterns were sturdy and bright, and travellers praised them.

One evening, a strange customer entered. He was a blind man, led by a dog. “I’d like to buy your best lantern,” he said.

Omar was puzzled. “Forgive me, sir, but why would a blind man need a lantern?”

The man smiled. “Because of other people. When I walk in the dark with a lantern, others can see me and avoid walking into me. My light is not for my own eyes. It’s a gift to everyone on the road.”

Omar was deeply moved. He gave the man the best lantern in the shop and refused to take any money. Afterwards, he often thought about the visitor. He had always seen his work as selling light to those who needed it, but the blind man had shown him a deeper truth: light has value when it is shared.

From then on, Omar left a lantern burning outside his shop every night, so that any lonely traveller could find their way, even without making a purchase. Strangely, his business doubled.

Moral: The light we carry helps not only ourselves but everyone who walks near us.

quiz.q: The strange customer was a blind man with a dog.
Omar asked the blind man to pay double.
Why did the blind man want a lantern?
o: So other people could see him in the dark

quiz.q: What did Omar do every night after that?
o: Left a lantern burning outside his shop
